title.en: Describe foreign exchange and trade reforms

say.en: Before 1991, a firm needed government permission even to make more of what it already made. What happens when those brakes are removed? In this lesson: Explain deregulation of industry.
Describe financial and tax reforms.
Describe foreign exchange and trade reforms.

body.en: Liberalisation means removing unnecessary controls on economic activity. Industrial licensing was abolished for almost all products except a few such as alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronics, aerospace, and drugs and pharmaceuticals. Only a few industries remain reserved for the public sector. In the *financial sector*, the RBI's role changed from regulator to facilitator; private and foreign banks were allowed, and the FDI limit in banks was raised to about 74 per cent.
body.kn: ಉದಾರೀಕರಣ ಎಂದರೆ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಗಳ ಮೇಲಿನ ಅನಗತ್ಯ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣಗಳನ್ನು ತೆಗೆಯುವುದು. ಕೆಲವು ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ಬಿಟ್ಟು ಉಳಿದೆಲ್ಲಕ್ಕೂ ಕೈಗಾರಿಕಾ ಪರವಾನಗಿ ರದ್ದಾಯಿತು. ಆರ್‌ಬಿಐ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಕದಿಂದ ಸಹಾಯಕನ ಪಾತ್ರಕ್ಕೆ ಬದಲಾಯಿತು.

Fewer industries reserved for the public *sector*
Foreign institutional investors allowed in Indian *financial* markets

title.en: On the board: Four areas of liberalisation

say.en: Liberalisation means removing unnecessary controls. It touched four areas.
Taxes were cut and simplified; GST came in July 2017. Trade lost its quantitative restrictions.
Devaluation: when 1 dollar goes from 20 to 25 rupees, a 500 rupee shirt falls from 25 to 20 dollars.
Indian goods become cheaper abroad, so exports are encouraged.

title.en: Tax, foreign exchange and trade reforms

body.en: Tax reforms reduced income tax and corporate tax rates and simplified procedures; the Goods and Services Tax, passed in 2016 and implemented from July 2017, created one indirect tax system for the country. The rupee was devalued in 1991 and its value is now largely market-determined. *Trade reforms* dismantled quantitative restrictions on imports and exports, reduced tariff rates and removed licensing for imports.
body.kn: ತೆರಿಗೆ ದರಗಳನ್ನು ಇಳಿಸಿ ಸರಳಗೊಳಿಸಲಾಯಿತು; ಜುಲೈ 2017ರಿಂದ ಸರಕು ಮತ್ತು ಸೇವಾ ತೆರಿಗೆ (ಜಿಎಸ್‌ಟಿ) ಜಾರಿಯಾಯಿತು. 1991ರಲ್ಲಿ ರೂಪಾಯಿ ಅಪಮೌಲ್ಯಗೊಳಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ಆಮದು-ರಫ್ತು ಮೇಲಿನ ಪರಿಮಾಣಾತ್ಮಕ ನಿರ್ಬಂಧಗಳನ್ನು ತೆಗೆಯಲಾಯಿತು.

points.en: GST: one nation, one tax, one market
Devaluation makes exports cheaper for *foreign* buyers

problem.en: Before devaluation $1 = ₹20. After devaluation $1 = ₹25. An Indian shirt costs ₹500. How much does it cost an American buyer before and after?

steps.en: The shirt is cheaper for foreigners, so exports are encouraged.

answer.en: $25 before, $20 after: devaluation makes Indian exports cheaper abroad.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Before devaluation $1 = ₹20. After devaluation $1 = ₹25. An Indian shirt costs ₹500. How much does it cost an American buyer before and after?

say.en: Let us work through this together. Before devaluation 1 equals 20 rupees. After devaluation 1 equals 25 rupees. An Indian shirt costs 500 rupees. How much does it cost an American buyer before and after?
Before: 500 divided by 20 = $25.
After: 500 divided by 25 = $20.
The shirt is cheaper for foreigners, so exports are encouraged.
So the answer is 25 before, 20 after: devaluation makes Indian exports cheaper abroad.
